CONTEXT: factory/reescalate.py is the hourly re-arm leg of the human-approval mailroom: it reads a card ledger (JSONL, last row per row_hash wins), selects rows whose status is in ELIGIBLE_STATUSES with a non-empty card_identifier, and re-buzzes the owner's phone for cards past their cadence. TODAY'S DEFECT (proven in production on 2026-08-05): a single malformed row — missing row_hash, or an eligible row missing both last_ping_at and first_raised — raises ReescalationError, which main() catches and turns into a whole-run abort (exit 2). One poisoned row silences re-arming for EVERY card until a human notices. Real example: rows for cards ANK-290..ANK-303 written 2026-08-01..03 had status open with no first_raised and stalled the entire lane.

CHANGE: per-row quarantine that stays fail-loud. Contract: (1) malformed rows (missing row_hash; eligible row with no usable cadence clock; any condition that currently raises per-row) are collected, not fatal — every OTHER card still gets evaluated and re-armed this run; (2) the quarantine is LOUD: print one line per quarantined row_hash/card with the exact reason to stdout, include a quarantined count in the run summary line, and exit with a distinct nonzero code (keep exit 2 for it) whenever any row was quarantined, so systemd still shows red and the deadman still fires — quarantine must never look like success; (3) quarantined rows are never pinged (a row you cannot reason about must not buzz the owner); (4) truly global failures (unreadable ledger file, malformed JSON making the whole file unparseable, config errors) still abort exactly as today — do not weaken those.

TESTS: update tests/test_reescalate.py deliberately: existing tests that pin the old all-abort behavior must be rewritten to pin the new contract (do not delete coverage — convert it). Add tests proving: (a) one malformed row + one due well-formed row => the well-formed card IS pinged AND exit code is nonzero AND the malformed row is named in output; (b) quarantined rows are not pinged; (c) unreadable ledger still aborts with no pings. Follow the file's existing test style and fixtures.

HOW TO RUN (from the worktree root — all must pass): PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_reescalate.py tests/test_reescalate_timer.py -q -p no:cacheprovider && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 loopfactory.py check

HARD RULES: no new dependencies, keep the deny-by-default posture (never invent an allow-on-failure path, never auto-approve, never downgrade urgency), no reformatting of untouched lines, never invoke any network, model CLI, MCP, or skill, and leave changes uncommitted — the harness exports the diff.
